items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I just saw Mat Domber’s son here in Clearwater.

ctx.x: You think there’s a future for this jazz party thing?

You know I don’t have the answer to that yet but occasionally I think about it. For example I just saw Mat Domber’s son here in Clearwater. I think his name is Jeff, sorry Jeff if it’s not Jeff. And I see the sons and daughters of the people who run the jazz party scenes. And I always say I wonder if so-and-so is going to take over when so-and-so is not here. So on that side I think it’s very possible. And then I say okay, now a lot of people that I know have passed on, audience members, listeners. So in that…

waned quite a bit. Now I’ve never done one of those Dick Gibson parties. And I used hear like those things were major, tons of people, a slew of musicians, it was a real party. I mean we used to hear about the crazy — in a good way crazy, you know musically and socially. But so everybody’s always talking about those days and how it’s dried up in a sense that way. And it probably has. And that’s why they try to introduce it to young people and try to get them in and things like that. But the jury’s out on that as…
